programme.title: The Brits Who Designed the Modern World
programme.desc: Brenda Emmanus presents profiles of 10 celebrated British designers whose work has revolutionised the nation's homes, streets and culture since the Second World War. Among those whose careers are highlighted are road-sign designer Margaret Calvert, ZX Spectrum creator Rick Dickinson, Andrew Ritchie, who gave the world the Brompton Bike, and Kenneth Grange, who designed everything from British Rail's distinctive InterCity 125 to Kenwood food mixers. A panel of contributors including Will.i.am, Jeremy Paxman, Pete Waterman and Ade Adepitan explain how their lives have benefited from British designs

programme.title: The Flying Gardener
programme.desc: Chris Beardshaw takes a helicopter ride to Kent, known as the Garden of England for its orchards, farms, hop fields and vineyards. In Whitstable, he meets a couple who are having trouble growing their own produce and need his help to turn their garden into a source of food for a family of five

programme.title: Close to Vermeer
programme.desc: Behind the scenes of the largest Vermeer exhibition ever mounted, now on view at the Rijksmuseum in Amsterdam. The documentary follows curators, conservators, collectors and experts in their joint mission to shine a new light on the elusive Dutch Master

programme.title: Archaeology: A Secret History
programme.desc: Richard Miles continues his series charting the history of archaeological breakthroughs by looking at how discoveries in the 18th and 19th centuries overturned previously formed ideas of when and where civilisation began, as empires competed to make their beliefs prevalent

programme.title: The Architecture the Railways Built
programme.desc: Tim Dunn explores the former HQ of London Underground, 55 Broadway, which was the capital's first skyscraper, and sees the timber-framed Barmouth Bridge in north Wales

programme.title: The Flying Gardener

programme.title: How the Celts Saved Britain
programme.desc: Conclusion. Dan Snow examines the ways in which the Celts saved Britain from cultural oblivion during the Dark Ages. He follows in the footsteps of Ireland's earliest missionaries as they ventured through treacherous barbarian territory, bringing literacy and technology to the future nations of Scotland and England

programme.title: Britain in Focus: A Photographic History
programme.desc: Eamonn McCabe traces the story of British photography, from the rapid innovation of Roger Fenton in the 1800s to the satirical eye of Martin Parr in the 21st century. Here he focuses on the explosion of colour images in the late 1950s through to the ongoing impact of the digital revolution

programme.title: I Am Martin Parr
programme.desc: A profile of the photographer, who revolutionised his art by inventing a political, humanist and accessible language. The programme follows him on a road trip, his camera trigger finger always at the ready to capture the smallest details of everyday life, and there are interviews with various individuals who have crossed paths with Parr, including close family, fellow photographers, artists and film-makers

programme.title: Rome's Invisible City
programme.desc: Alexander Armstrong is joined by Dr Michael Scott to explore the underground treasures that made Rome the powerhouse of the ancient world. Using 3D scanning technology, he uncovers the lost subterranean world of the Colosseum, as well as the aqueducts and sewers that supplied and cleansed it, and helped run civilisation's first metropolis and its empire

programme.title: Fred Dibnah's Building of Britain
programme.desc: Fred uncovers the construction techniques of stonemasons and carpenters through the ages, focusing on Norman cathedrals. The former steeplejack admires Peterborough Cathedral and Rochester Castle, where he demonstrates how tactics used to invade the fortress centuries ago resemble today's demolition methods

programme.title: Villages by the Sea
programme.desc: Archaeologist Ben Robinson travels to Seaton Sluice in Northumberland, home to the notorious Delaval family. These wealthy bottle-makers were some of the greatest players on the Georgian party scene. Their pranks and parties were infamous at their impressive mansion, but they also brought great innovation to the area, when they redesigned the harbour

programme.title: Rome: A History of the Eternal City
programme.desc: Simon Sebag Montefiore charts Rome's rise from the abandonment and neglect of the 14th century into the everlasting seat of the Papacy recognised today. His story begins with the debauchery and decadence of the Renaissance, and takes viewers through the Catholic Reformation and on to the arrival of fascism and the creation of the Vatican State. He steps inside sensational palaces and churches, and talks about some of the world's most beloved art as he brings his exploration of Rome to a close

programme.desc: As Claudius continues his conquest of Britain, Messalina runs wild with lust. After competing in a tournament of sex, in which she takes on the champion of the Guild of Prostitutes, Sylla, she begins a rebellion of her own. However, her decision to proceed with a divorce and publicly marry new lover Silius leads to disastrous consequences. Derek Jacobi and Sheila White star

programme.title: I, Claudius
programme.desc: As he approaches the end of his years, Claudius is urged to re-marry and decides upon the scheming Agrippinilla as his new spouse - despite knowing she will try to make her son Nero the emperor. Derek Jacobi stars

programme.title: The Australian Wars
programme.desc: Rachel Perkins examines the British Empire's abolition of slavery and how abolitionists attempted to negotiate treaties with the indigenous people. She focuses on the downfall of these treaties due to settler interests and how this killed around 72,000 Aboriginal people with the Native Police, assigned by the new government, moving north. In the north and west the pattern is repeated, a process of quieting blacks begins, also known as the 'killing times'

programme.desc: Maria, Shane and Jim arrive at hospital, where Danny is having his stomach pumped. Scott, Jim and Max confront Pete and report him to the police.

programme.title: Neighbours
programme.desc: Harry returns with a different girlfriend. Max helps Des with some plumbing. Danny asks Max for the $500 owed for damages to the Hall, and Shane sells his diving trophies to raise the money.

programme.title: Sister Boniface Mysteries
programme.desc: Grace Pearson is found dead at a local festival. Detective Inspector Sam Gillespie - to the bewilderment of newly arrived Detective Sergeant Felix Livingstone - uses Sister Boniface as his scientific adviser. She determines that Pearson died by suffocation after her head was pushed into sawdust. The investigation leads to the three Bellamy siblings, at whose home Pearson was a housemaid. Crime drama, starring Lorna Watson and Max Brown, with Belinda Lang and Robert Daws

programme.title: Kingdom
programme.desc: When Peter refuses to post bail for Simon, Lyle manages to secure his release using a case of money left behind when he was arrested. A well-to-do woman seeks the services of Kingdom and Kingdom to force an American pilot to support her unborn baby - but investigations reveal neither party is being completely honest

programme.title: As Time Goes By

programme.title: Last of the Summer Wine

programme.title: Last of the Summer Wine
programme.desc: An afternoon driving around in Wesley's car proves to be tough on the feet. Compo is suffering from hard skin and places his faith in a herbal jelly from a gypsy healer. Bill Owen stars

programme.title: Last of the Summer Wine
programme.desc: Clegg and Seymour visit an old friend in hospital following his hernia operation and go to extraordinary lengths to cheer him up. Peter Sallis and Michael Aldridge star in the first episode to feature Clem 'Smiler' Hemmingway (Stephen Lewis)

programme.title: The Chelsea Detective
programme.desc: Part one of two. When antiques dealer Niall Hammond is found dead, Max and Layla begin a curious case involving a prestigious music society and mudlarks on the Thames foreshore

programme.title: The Chelsea Detective

programme.title: New Tricks
programme.desc: As the Gibraltar locals reel from the murder of shipping agent Gordon Fletcher, Brian and Gerry - last seen being carried off in a shipping container - find themselves stranded on the side of a Spanish mountain, and now face the problem of how to get back to the rest of the team. As Sandra attempts to unravel secrets stretching back over three decades and link what has now become three murders, she still has doubts about the innocence of charming entrepreneur Harry Truman - but that doesn't stop her joining him for lunch on his luxury yacht. Conclusion of a two-part story, with regulars Amanda Redman, Alun Armstrong, Dennis Waterman and Denis Lawson joined by Vincent Regan and George Irving

programme.sub-title: In the Hands of an Angry God

programme.title: D-Day to Berlin
programme.desc: The last few months of the Second World War, when decisions were made that would determine the shape of Europe for several decades. The programme examines the final battles inside Germany, the assault on Berlin and the events that led to Hitler's death - not least the emergence of a new dictator in the person of Soviet leader Josef Stalin. Featuring testimony from veterans, archive footage and dramatic reconstruction. Narrated by Sean Bean

programme.title: D-Day: The Last Heroes
programme.desc: Historian Dan Snow presents the first of a two-part documentary examining how two years of meticulous planning, espionage and the analysis of millions of 3D aerial photographs helped the Allied forces gain a foothold in northern France during the Second World War. He reveals how the June 1944 landings were conducted in two phases, an airborne assault and an amphibious landing. The essential element of surprise was upheld with some help from inclement weather and a comprehensive deception plan

programme.title: D-Day: The Last Heroes
programme.desc: The concluding part of historian Dan Snow's documentary tells the powerful and heroic stories of those who risked their lives on the beaches of Normandy to save the world from Nazi Germany

programme.title: Fake or Fortune?
programme.desc: Helen McNicoll was one of Canada's most celebrated female artists of the early 20th century. Fiona Bruce and Philip Mould investigate a picturesque outdoor scene of women in a field sold at auction in England in the artist's style. The picture was bought at auction by artist and small-time art dealer David Taylor for £2,000, but it could be worth more than £300,000 if truly painted by McNicoll - can the team help prove it's the real thing?

programme.title: Fake or Fortune?
programme.desc: Journalist Fiona Bruce and art expert Philip Mould take on the fast-growing market for rock music memorabilia. They set out to demonstrate whether a Hawaiian steel guitar called 'Silver Queen' once belonged to Ronnie Wood of the Rolling Stones and prove that a baby grand piano now owned by '90s pop star Chesney Hawkes once belonged to John Lennon of the Beatles

programme.title: Fake or Fortune?
programme.desc: Presenter Fiona Bruce and art expert Philip Mould investigate a dreamlike landscape painting, purported to be by one of the forefathers of Impressionism and one of the most important artists of the 19th century, Jean-Baptiste-Camille Corot. The picture was purchased in the 1970s by Sally Green's late husband Derek, a country antiques dealer, primarily for its impressive frame. Derek was always intrigued by the painting and wondered whether or not it was genuine. Sally is now on a mission to finish what he started. However, the painting was previously turned down by leading experts on Corot's work, so Fiona and Philip have to find new evidence to help persuade them to change their minds

programme.title: Trawlermen: Hunting the Catch
programme.desc: Documentary charting the contrasting fortunes of British fishing boats over the course of one brutal week. Meanwhile, off the Yorkshire coast, crabber Tydus welcomes a greenhorn to the crew

programme.title: Patagonia: Earth's Secret Paradise
programme.desc: Life in the treacherous seas that surround the South American wilderness. The 4,000-mile coast stretches from the cold waters of Cape Horn - where rockhopper penguins overcome huge challenges to raise their young - to the far north's much warmer climate, where huge elephant seals battle for position in the heat of the desert. Orcas ram-raid the beaches, grabbing seal pups to feed their young, and fishermen are also incentivised to gather the sea's bounty. Narrated by Santiago Cabrera

programme.title: Fake or Fortune?
programme.desc: Helen McNicoll was one of Canada's most celebrated female artists of the early 20th century. Fiona Bruce and Philip Mould investigate a picturesque outdoor scene of women in a field sold at auction in England in the artist's style. The picture was bought at auction by artist and small-time art dealer David Taylor for £2,000, but it could be worth more than £300,000 if truly painted by McNicoll - can the team help prove it's the real thing?

programme.title: Fake or Fortune?
programme.desc: Journalist Fiona Bruce and art expert Philip Mould take on the fast-growing market for rock music memorabilia. They set out to demonstrate whether a Hawaiian steel guitar called 'Silver Queen' once belonged to Ronnie Wood of the Rolling Stones and prove that a baby grand piano now owned by '90s pop star Chesney Hawkes once belonged to John Lennon of the Beatles

programme.title: Fake or Fortune?
programme.desc: Presenter Fiona Bruce and art expert Philip Mould investigate a dreamlike landscape painting, purported to be by one of the forefathers of Impressionism and one of the most important artists of the 19th century, Jean-Baptiste-Camille Corot. The picture was purchased in the 1970s by Sally Green's late husband Derek, a country antiques dealer, primarily for its impressive frame. Derek was always intrigued by the painting and wondered whether or not it was genuine. Sally is now on a mission to finish what he started. However, the painting was previously turned down by leading experts on Corot's work, so Fiona and Philip have to find new evidence to help persuade them to change their minds

programme.desc: David Attenborough highlights the curiosities that have led to accusations of forgery, but have ultimately helped assist the rethinking of evolution. programme.title: DIY SOS
programme.desc: Nick Knowles travels to the Isle of Sheppey in Kent to meet two extraordinary dads, Garry and Kyle, who have adopted four vulnerable children - three of whom have special needs - to give them the best life possible. So to give this family the space they so desperately need, the DIY SOS builders are undertaking their most ambitious project yet - to demolish the bungalow and build a bespoke five-bedroom house in its place. programme.desc: The veteran journalist tells the extraordinary untold story of how the two most notorious women in British crime, Rose West and Myra Hindley, became lesbian lovers in jail. Former Category A prisoners, including reformed Mafia member Marisa Merico and ex-gangster Linda Calvey, tell Sir Trevor how Rose West revealed her murderous temper in prison, while former prison governor Veronica Bird, police officers and prison visitors describe how Hindley cleverly manipulated people in jail, even persuading a female guard to help her escape

programme.title: Serial Killer with Piers Morgan

Although Riebe has since withdrawn his confessions, police believe he is one of the worst serial killers in Florida's history. Piers uses Riebe's video and audio confessions, news archive and testimony to explore what sort of man would commit murder and then taunt the victims' families for nearly 20 years

programme.title: Serial Killer with Piers Morgan
programme.desc: The broadcaster meets Bronx businessman Alex Henriquez, who was convicted for three murders in 1992. The victims had two things in common - they were all asphyxiated before being dumped by the highway and all three could be placed with Alex Henriquez shortly before their deaths. For 30 years the killer has protested his innocence, claiming the police set him up. Piers Morgan tries to uncover the truth
